items.title: Texas AG Ken Paxton launches investigations into UnitedHealth Group, BCBSTX
items.reason: This reports a regulatory enforcement action by a state attorney general against major payers (UnitedHealth Group and BCBSTX) for alleged deceptive practices and care denial, which directly matches the payer litigation and enforcement topic definition.
items.summary: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton announced an investigation into UnitedHealth Group and BCBSTX for allegedly engaging in deceptive and unlawful practices that may have resulted in denied care to Texas residents. This state-level regulatory enforcement action targets two major national payers and addresses potential claims-denial practices, directly impacting revenue-cycle operations through potential policy changes, settlement requirements, or operational compliance mandates that could affect claim processing and payment practices in the Texas market.

items.title: Independence Blue Cross to pay $22.5M in Medicare Advantage inaccurate diagnoses allegations settlement
items.reason: This is a CMS enforcement action and settlement against a major Blue Cross payer (Independence Blue Cross) involving Medicare Advantage claims and allegations of submitting inaccurate diagnosis data—a core payer enforcement matter directly affecting revenue-cycle operations and claim adjudication.
items.summary: Independence Blue Cross agreed to pay $22.5 million to settle CMS allegations that it submitted inaccurate and untruthful diagnosis data to Medicare for Medicare Advantage beneficiaries between 2017 and 2021. The settlement resolves claims that the payer incorrectly reported patient diagnoses to justify higher risk-adjustment payments. This enforcement action against a major BCBS carrier demonstrates CMS scrutiny of diagnosis coding accuracy in MA plans and creates liability exposure for payers that may influence future claims submission practices and provider audit standards affecting revenue-cycle teams.

This litigation is relevant to revenue-cycle teams because outcomes could reshape how CMS conducts Medicare Advantage compliance audits and enforcement actions that directly affect payer operations and claims processing requirements.
